title: Software Technology Parks Strengthen India’s IT Export Ecosystem and Ease of Doing Business
subtitle: STP Units Record over ₹7.73 Lakh Crore in Exports in FY 2025-26
body_text:
The Government of India has launched several initiatives and programs to support the expansion of the IT sector and is constantly working to promote the sector throughout the country. The Software Technology Park (STP) is one such important scheme in this effort.
STP Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme to promote software and IT-enabled services (IT/ITeS) exports from India and STPI has been providing Statutory Services on a single-window Clearance System under STP Scheme.

STPI adheres to the prescribed timelines for approvals and delivery of services under the STP Scheme, as outlined in its Citizen’s Charter available at https://stpi.in/en/citizens-charter .
Measures taken by the Software technology Parks of India (STPI) to streamline approvals and improve ease of doing business for STP units are as follows:
Automation of Statutory Services: For providing seamless services to the IT exporters, statutory services including SOFTEX filling, its approval and final intimation to them has been automated. This has ensured speedy delivery of services to the satisfaction of the IT industry. Integration with RBI’s Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) System for IT exporters: STPI’s online system for IT exporters has been integrated with the Reserve Bank of India’s EDPMS for sharing of export data. This integration has enabled seamless electronic transmission of export declaration data to RBI in near real time. This has facilitated faster exchange of export data, enhanced accuracy and transparency, reduced manual intervention, improved monitoring of export transactions, and streamlined regulatory compliance for IT/ITeS exporters. Simplification of Import Procedures: The earlier practice of case-to-case import permissions has been replaced with blanket import permissions for the financial year concerned. Self-Declaration for Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) Sales: The requirement for prior DTA permissions for STPI-registered units has been replaced with a submission of self-declaration (except for advance DTA sales in first year of operation).
This information was given by Union Minister of Electronics and IT Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Lok Sabha on 12.08.2026

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply dated 12 August 2026, the Minister of Electronics and IT informed Parliament that Software Technology Park (STP) units recorded exports of over ₹7.73 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, up from ₹6.88 lakh crore in FY 2024-25. The number of registered STP units rose to 2,125 in FY 2025-26, with Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra leading in both unit count and export value. The release also listed ease-of-doing-business measures taken by STPI, including automation of SOFTEX filing, integration with RBI's EDPMS system, blanket import permissions, and self-declaration for DTA sales.
enrichment.context:
The Software Technology Park (STP) Scheme, administered by Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) under MeitY, is a 100% export-oriented scheme launched in 1991 to promote software and IT/ITeS exports through a single-window statutory clearance mechanism, including SOFTEX certification (mandatory for realizing export proceeds in foreign exchange) and customs/import facilitation. Unlike SEZ units, STP units can operate from anywhere, including non-SEZ premises, making the scheme particularly important for smaller cities and tier-2/3 towns where STPI has extended IT infrastructure to promote regional balance in IT exports (e.g., growth in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh).

This release is significant in the context of India's digital economy push and Ease of Doing Business rankings, as it highlights procedural simplifications—automation, RBI-EDPMS integration, blanket import permissions—that reduce compliance burden for IT exporters. It also reflects continued dominance of a few states (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Telangana) in IT/ITeS exports, relevant to discussions on regional disparities in India's digital economy. However, as a routine parliamentary answer providing periodic statistics rather than announcing a new policy or scheme, its primary value lies in data awareness rather than being a landmark development.

prelims_questions.question: The Software Technology Park (STP) Scheme, administered by STPI, is best described as:
options: A scheme providing subsidies for domestic software consumption
A 100% export-oriented scheme for promoting IT/ITeS exports through single-window statutory clearances
A scheme exclusively for units located within Special Economic Zones
A credit guarantee scheme for software startups
prelims_questions.explanation: As stated in the release, the STP Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme to promote software and IT-enabled services (IT/ITeS) exports, with STPI providing statutory services under a single-window clearance system.

prelims_questions.question: SOFTEX filing, mentioned in the context of STPI's services, is primarily related to:
options: Certification of software export value for foreign exchange realization
Allocation of spectrum for IT companies
prelims_questions.explanation: SOFTEX is a certification/declaration form used by software exporters to report export value, which STPI processes and shares with RBI (via EDPMS) for foreign exchange realization and regulatory compliance.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of the Software Technology Park (STP) Scheme in promoting India's IT/ITeS export ecosystem. How have recent procedural reforms by STPI contributed to improving ease of doing business for IT exporters?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Economy: Infrastructure and Services

mains_questions.question: India's IT exports remain heavily concentrated in a few states. Analyze the regional disparities in India's digital economy and suggest measures to promote balanced growth of the IT/ITeS sector across states.
